concept: Turkish conquest of India Ghaznavid Muhammad Ghuri
question: In the 11th century, under Maḥmūd of Ghazni, Ghaznī, a small town in ______, became the capital of the vast empire of the Ghaznavids.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Afghanistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni **defeated** Hindushahis** to conquer and annex Peshawar and Punjab.
 
• Maḥmūd is said to have vowed to invade India once a year and, in fact, led about **17 such expeditions.**
 
• The **first large-scale** campaign **began in 1001 **and the last **ended in 1026**.
 
• **In 1001,** Maḥmūd marched on India and **defeated Jaipal,** the king of Punjab.
 
• Maḥmūd was the** first to carry the banner of Islam** into the heart of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ottoman Empire** in Turkiye was Founded by **Osman I in 1299**, the Ottoman Empire became one of the most powerful empires in history.
 
• After the fall of the Ottoman Empire post-WWI, **Mustafa Kemal Atatürk** founded the Republic of Turkiye in 1923
 
• **Alexander the Great** Conquered Egypt in 332 BCE, leading to the establishment of the **Ptolemaic Kingdom**.
 
• **Library of Alexandria** Became a center of learning and culture in the **Hellenistic world**.
 
• **Zoroastrianism** the predominant religion, founded by the **prophet Zoroaster**, emphasizing the duality of good and evil came from Persia.
